features.title: Features
features.description: What LocalGateKeys does, edition by edition: encrypted vault, browser and desktop fill, passkeys, Windows Hello, two-factor codes, imports, backups and device sync.
features.everything-it-does-and.1: Everything it does, and where it does it
features.everything-it-does-and.2: All of this runs on your own devices. Free holds up to 4 items; Pro removes the limit and adds sync, two-factor codes and documents.
features.everything-it-does-and.3: The LocalGateKeys Home page: password health, upcoming reminders, a one-time codes card with live two-factor codes, and a list of logins with site logos.
features.everything-it-does-and.4: Home: password health, reminders, live two-factor codes and your items. Demo vault with made-up accounts.
features.the-vault.3: Everything you save is encrypted with a key protected by your master password, using Argon2id and AES-256-GCM. Names, usernames and websites are encrypted too, not just passwords.
features.the-vault.5: Website and desktop app logins, passkeys, payment cards, bank accounts, identities, secure notes, documents, SSH keys, API keys, Wi-Fi networks, bookmarks, software licences, subscriptions, warranties and purchases, each with its own fields.
features.the-vault.7: Keep files such as scanned documents in the vault, up to 25 MB each. Each file is encrypted with its own key. You can preview a document, save a copy, or open it in another app.
features.the-vault.9: Store a site's setup key and LocalGateKeys shows the current code at the top of the login, and on a One-time codes card on the Home page. Codes follow the TOTP standard (RFC 6238): 6 to 8 digits, 15 to 120 seconds, SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512.
features.the-vault.10: Add a code from a QR code
features.the-vault.11: Snip the QR code on the site's two-factor setup page with Win+Shift+S and paste it, or hold it up to your webcam. A Google Authenticator export QR code works too. The image is read on your PC and never saved.
features.the-vault.13: Random passwords of 8 to 256 characters, or passphrases of 3 to 16 words.
features.the-vault.15: See which saved passwords are weak, reused, more than a year old or missing a two-factor code. Breach checks against Have I Been Pwned are off until you turn them on, run only when you start them, and send only five characters of a hash, never the password.
features.the-vault.17: Each item shows the site's icon, a built-in logo for well-known sites, or an icon for its kind, so you can spot it at a glance.
features.the-vault.19: Find items with a command palette (Ctrl+K), filter chips, favourites and your own collections. Arrow keys, Enter and Ctrl+C work in the item list straight from the search box.
features.the-vault.21: Deleted items go to the trash, and the message that confirms it has an Undo button. The trash empties itself after 30 days, or keeps everything until you empty it.
features.the-vault.23: When a login's password changes, the last five old passwords are kept in its encrypted history.
features.the-vault.24: A GitHub login open in LocalGateKeys, with its current two-factor code at the top, then username, hidden password, website, notes and recovery codes.
features.the-vault.25: The current two-factor code sits at the top of the login.
features.the-vault.26: The password generator with a random 20-character password and options for length, letters, digits and symbols.
features.the-vault.27: The generator makes random passwords or passphrases.
features.the-vault.28: The Security center showing a score of 77 out of 100, with weak, reused, no two-factor and old passwords to review, and unlock and backup checks.
features.the-vault.29: The Security center lists what to fix first.
features.moving-in-and-out.3: Bring in exports from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Proton Pass, KeePass and KeePassXC (including .kdbx files), Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox and Safari, or any other CSV file. You review every item before anything is written, and the import never goes online.
features.moving-in-and-out.5: Export to an encrypted KeePass KDBX 4 file, or to Bitwarden-compatible CSV or JSON, or KeePass XML. Every export asks for your master password first.
features.filling-sign-ins.3: Fill and save logins on websites, including sign-ins that ask for the username and password on separate pages. The extension asks the app on your PC for logins that match the exact site, through a local helper. It also fills two-factor codes, addresses and payment cards.
features.filling-sign-ins.5: After you sign in, the extension offers to save a new login or update a changed password. You can turn the prompt off for any site from the toolbar button.
features.filling-sign-ins.7: Nothing is filled until you pick an account. Forms are not submitted for you unless you turn on "Sign in after filling" in Settings, and then only after a fill you started.
features.filling-sign-ins.9: When a website in Chrome or Edge offers a passkey, LocalGateKeys can save it in your vault and sign you in with it. You approve every passkey in the desktop app, with Windows Hello or your master password, and the browser's own passkey dialog is always one click away. The private key never leaves the app.
features.filling-sign-ins.11: Fill sign-in windows of Windows programs with a fill button beside the password field or a hotkey (Ctrl+Shift+Space). Each app is bound once, and fill is refused if the program, its window or its fields have changed since.
features.filling-sign-ins.13: Search your vault and copy from anywhere with a hotkey (Ctrl+Alt+K by default). Ctrl+Alt+L locks the vault at once.
features.filling-sign-ins.15: LocalGateKeys installs no keyboard hook, reads no screen content to find passwords, and injects nothing into other programs. If an app does not expose proper sign-in fields, it is not filled.
features.filling-sign-ins.16: A sign-in page with the LocalGateKeys browser extension offering two saved accounts for that site.
features.filling-sign-ins.17: The extension offers only the logins saved for the site you are on.
features.unlocking.3: At least 12 characters, never written to disk. It is the one thing that opens your vault, and we cannot reset it.
features.unlocking.5: Unlock with your fingerprint, face or PIN through Windows Hello, after you set it up in LocalGateKeys.
features.unlocking.7: An optional webcam face check for PCs without Windows Hello. It is a convenience, not certified anti-spoofing; prefer Windows Hello when you can.
features.unlocking.9: An optional 24-word phrase that can open the vault if you forget the master password. It is shown once and never stored by the app.
features.unlocking.11: The vault locks after a period you choose, and copied passwords are cleared from the clipboard. Only what LocalGateKeys copied is cleared.
features.backups.3: Daily or weekly, at a time you set. Each backup is a full encrypted file, checked after writing, with attachments included.
features.backups.4: Extra copy in a folder you choose
features.backups.5: Have each backup copied to a OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox or Proton Drive folder, or anywhere else. Only encrypted backup files are copied, never the live vault.
features.backups.7: Move selected items to another vault in an encrypted file protected by its own password.
features.sync-between-your-devices.3: Pair a PC once with a one-use QR code (between PCs you paste its text). When both are unlocked on the same network, they exchange changes directly over an authenticated, encrypted connection. Nothing goes through the internet.
features.sync-between-your-devices.5: If your PCs are rarely on the same network, sync through a OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive or iCloud Drive folder you already use, protected by a sync password. The provider only ever stores encrypted files. You can use both routes.
features.sync-between-your-devices.7: Website and desktop app logins, and other items such as notes and bookmarks. Collections, documents and attachments do not sync yet. Edits made on two PCs at once keep both versions, and a delete moves the item to the trash on the other PCs.
features.sync-between-your-devices.9: The iPhone app syncs with your Windows PC. Get it on the App Store.An iPhone app is coming. It will sync with your Windows PC. It is not available yet.
features.privacy.3: You never sign up or sign in. A Pro licence is a key you keep, checked on your PC.
features.privacy.5: The app sends no usage data, crash reports or analytics.
features.privacy.7: On by default. It blocks background internet requests and breach checks, and an update check asks you first.
features.privacy.9: To show a site's icon, the app downloads it from that site. This tells the site you have an account there, and nothing else. It is off by default: turn on "Show website icons" in Settings (strict offline mode must be off).
features.privacy.11: Checking for updates downloads one small signed file. The app never downloads or installs anything by itself.
get_started.title: Get started
get_started.description: How to install LocalGateKeys on Windows, set up your vault, add the browser extension for Edge or Chrome, and what to expect for iPhone and Android.
get_started.get-started.2: Install the Windows app, create your vault, then add the browser extension. It takes about five minutes, and you never need an account.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.2: LocalGateKeys runs on Windows 10 and Windows 11, 64-bit. Pick one way to install it:
get_started.1-install-the-windows.3: Microsoft Store (recommended). The Store installs it and keeps it up to date. Open LocalGateKeys in the Microsoft Store, choose Get, then Open.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.4: Installer. Download it from the download page, check its SHA-256 as shown there, and run it. Windows SmartScreen may warn you because the installer is not code-signed yet: if the fingerprint matches, choose More info, then Run anyway.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.5: Use only one of the two on a PC.
get_started.1-install-the-windows.6: Get it from the Microsoft Store
get_started.2-create-your-vault.2: Open LocalGateKeys. On first start it asks you to create a vault.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.3: Choose a master password of at least 12 characters. Write it down and keep it somewhere safe. We never have it, so nobody can reset it for you.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.4: Open Security center in the sidebar and set up a recovery phrase. Keep it offline, for example on paper. It opens the vault if you forget the master password.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.5: In the same place, turn on Windows Hello if your PC has a fingerprint reader, a Hello camera or a PIN, so day-to-day unlocking is quick.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.6: Turn on scheduled backups in Settings and choose where the encrypted backup files go, such as a USB drive or a folder you already back up.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.7: The Security center with the password health score, items to fix, and the unlock and backup settings: master password, Windows Hello, recovery phrase, auto-lock and backups.
get_started.2-create-your-vault.8: The Security center keeps unlock methods, the recovery phrase and backups in one place.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.2: The extension fills sign-ins in your browser. It talks only to the LocalGateKeys app on the same PC, so install the app first.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.4: Microsoft Edge: open it in Edge Add-ons and choose Get.coming soon.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.5: Google Chrome: open it in the Chrome Web Store and choose Add to Chrome.coming soon to the Chrome Web Store.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.6: Pin it: open the browser's extensions menu (the puzzle-piece icon) and pin LocalGateKeys to the toolbar.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.7: Keep the app running and unlocked. Go to a sign-in page you have a login saved for: the extension offers only the logins saved for that exact site. Nothing fills until you click.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.8: Sign in somewhere new and the extension offers to save the login.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.9: Extension says it cannot reach the app? In the app, open Devices & connections and choose Repair bridge, then restart the browser.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.10: A sign-in page with the LocalGateKeys browser extension offering two saved accounts for that site.
get_started.3-add-the-browser.11: The extension offers only the logins saved for the site you are on.
get_started.4-bring-your-passwords.2: Choose Import & export in the sidebar and pick an export file from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Proton Pass, KeePass or KeePassXC, Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox or Safari, or any CSV. You review every item before anything is saved, and nothing goes online. Delete the export file afterwards, because most exports hold passwords in plain text.
get_started.4-bring-your-passwords.3: The free edition holds up to 4 items. Pro removes the limit.
get_started.5-fill-windows-apps.2: For programs such as game launchers, open a desktop login in the app and choose App binding… to bind it to the program's sign-in window once. After that, a fill button appears beside the password field, or you can use the hotkey. LocalGateKeys refuses to fill if the program or window has changed since you bound it.
get_started.6-turn-on-pro.2: Pro is a single payment that adds unlimited items, sync between your devices, two-factor codes and documents. After you buy it, paste your licence key in Tools > Licence in the app. See your Pro licence.
get_started.iphone-and-android.2: iPhone: install LocalGateKeys from the App Store. It syncs with your Windows PC.an iPhone app that syncs with your Windows PC is in development. It is not available yet.
get_started.iphone-and-android.3: Android: an Android app is planned. It is not available yet.
get_started.iphone-and-android.4: Setup steps for <!-- if:IPHONE_APP_URL -->Android<!-- else -->both<!-- /if --> will appear on this page when <!-- if:IPHONE_APP_URL -->the app is<!-- else -->each app is<!-- /if --> released. Until then, your vault stays on your PC, and you can sync between Windows PCs with Pro.
get_started.iphone-and-android.5: Stuck? See Support and FAQ or email {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}.

index.title: LocalGateKeys
index.description: A password manager for Windows that keeps your encrypted vault on your own devices. No account, no LocalGateKeys server, no telemetry.
index.a-password-manager-that.1: A password manager that stays on your PC.
index.a-password-manager-that.2: Your vault lives on your devices. We never see it. You choose whether encrypted copies travel through your home Wi-Fi, your own cloud folder, or nowhere.
index.a-password-manager-that.7: Get it from the Microsoft Store
index.a-password-manager-that.13: Your vault sits at the centre, on your PC. The inner ring is your home Wi-Fi, where a second PC can sync directly; an iPhone app is <!-- if:IPHONE_APP_URL -->on the App Store<!-- else -->in development<!-- /if -->. The outer ring is your own cloud folder, which only ever holds encrypted files. LocalGateKeys servers are outside both rings and never see your vault.

security.title: Security
security.description: How LocalGateKeys protects your vault and what it does not protect against.
security.the-security-model-in.1: The security model, in plain terms
security.the-security-model-in.2: What LocalGateKeys is designed to protect, and what it cannot protect.
security.how-your-vault-is.2: A random 256-bit key encrypts the vault. That key is never stored as it is; it is wrapped (encrypted) separately by each way you can unlock, so changing your password does not mean re-encrypting everything, and a wrapper copied from another vault is rejected.
security.how-your-vault-is.4: AES-256-GCM with a fresh random nonce for every save
security.how-your-vault-is.6: Argon2id, 64 MiB memory, 3 passes, parallelism 4, random salt per wrapper
security.how-your-vault-is.8: Optional 24-word BIP39 phrase (256 bits), expanded with HKDF-SHA256
security.how-your-vault-is.10: Wraps the vault key, never the master password
security.how-your-vault-is.12: Argon2id and AES-256-GCM with the parameters stored in the authenticated header
security.how-your-vault-is.14: A random group key, handed to each device with X25519 and HKDF-SHA256 and, for a cloud folder, also wrapped by your sync password with Argon2id; every record sealed with AES-256-GCM and bound to its item, version and key epoch; every device file bound to the device that wrote it
security.how-your-vault-is.16: ES256 (P-256) keys kept inside the encrypted vault; the app builds the signed data from the origin the browser reports, never from the page
security.how-your-vault-is.18: Temporary file, flush, then atomic replace, so a crash cannot leave half a vault
security.designed-to-protect-against.2: Someone who copies your vault file or a backup and does not know your master password
security.designed-to-protect-against.3: A website getting logins or passkeys saved for a different website
security.designed-to-protect-against.4: Another program on your PC talking to LocalGateKeys without the session secret it hands to its own browser helper
security.designed-to-protect-against.5: Filling a desktop app that has been swapped, updated or changed since you bound it
security.designed-to-protect-against.8: Your cloud provider reading synced data: it only stores ciphertext
security.not-able-to-protect.2: Malware, or anyone with administrator control, already running on your PC
security.not-able-to-protect.3: A compromised browser, Windows installation or dependency
security.not-able-to-protect.4: A website you deliberately fill a password into
security.not-able-to-protect.5: Someone using your PC while the vault is unlocked
security.not-able-to-protect.6: Phishing inside a genuine app that shows attacker-controlled content
security.not-able-to-protect.7: Losing your vault, your backups and your master password with no recovery phrase: nobody, including us, can open it
security.things-localgatekeys-never-does: Some ways of filling passwords are indistinguishable from spyware, so they are ruled out by design. LocalGateKeys contains no:
screen reading or OCR to find credentials
decryption of your browser's saved-password database
code injection into other programs or games
submitting a sign-in you did not start
security.the-network-honestly.2: There is no LocalGateKeys account and no server that holds vaults. The app connects to the internet in only these cases:
security.the-network-honestly.3: Update checks. When you choose Check for updates, the app downloads one small file and verifies its signature with a key built into the app. It never downloads or runs an installer by itself.
security.the-network-honestly.4: Licence revocation list. Together with each update check, the app downloads a signed list of refunded licences and checks your licence against it on your PC. It sends nothing about your licence.
security.the-network-honestly.5: Website icons. To show a site's icon, the app downloads it from that site's own address. No username, password or vault data is sent, but each download tells that site, and anyone watching the network, that your vault has an account there. This is off by default and only happens if you turn on "Show website icons" in Settings; strict offline mode blocks it.
security.the-network-honestly.6: Breach checks, if you turn them on. When you start a check, the app sends the first five characters of each password's SHA-1 hash to Have I Been Pwned. The service sees your IP address, never the password, the full hash, the username or the website.
security.the-network-honestly.7: Sync, if you set it up. Over your home network, devices talk to each other directly. Through a cloud folder, your cloud-drive app does the uploading.
security.the-network-honestly.8: Strict offline mode is on by default. It blocks background internet requests, website icons and breach checks, and an update check asks you first. The privacy policy lists exactly what our servers see when you do check for updates.
security.known-limitations.2: The master password is moved into a wipeable buffer as soon as it reaches the app and is erased when the operation that needed it finishes. The page you type it into runs in Microsoft Edge WebView2, and the hand-off from that page to the app makes a short-lived copy; neither copy can be erased by the app.
security.known-limitations.3: The camera unlock is a convenience check, not certified protection against photos or masks. Windows Hello is the stronger choice.
security.known-limitations.4: Windows app fill does not work with programs running as administrator, custom-drawn game interfaces, or embedded web views it cannot verify.
security.known-limitations.5: The vault detects being rolled back to an older copy. If you use sync, your other devices also remember how new your vault was, so deleting the vault and its anchor file together is caught at the next sync (Windows PCs for now; the iPhone, Mac and Android apps follow). Without sync, someone who can replace both files can still defeat the check.
security.known-limitations.6: Passkeys work in Chrome and Edge only, and only for the page itself: a sign-in inside another site's frame uses the browser's own passkey dialog. If a site cancels after you approve a new passkey, the passkey may stay in your vault; delete it in the app.
security.report-a-vulnerability.2: Email {{SECURITY_EMAIL}}. The vulnerability disclosure policy explains what is in scope, how quickly we respond and how we credit researchers.
support.title: Support and FAQ
support.description: Answers to common questions about LocalGateKeys, master passwords, Pro licences, sync and refunds, and how to contact support.
support.support-and-questions.2: Most answers are below. For anything else, email {{CONTACT_EMAIL}}. Never send us your master password, recovery phrase or vault file; we will never ask for them.
support.your-vault.2: I forgot my master password. Can you reset it?
support.your-vault.3: No. We never have your master password or your vault, so there is nothing we could reset. If you created a recovery phrase, use it on the unlock screen to open the vault and set a new password.
support.your-vault.4: Without the password or the recovery phrase, the vault cannot be opened by anyone. Backups are encrypted with their own backup password, so a backup you can still open is the other way back in.
support.your-vault.5: Do you keep a copy of my vault?
support.your-vault.6: No. There is no LocalGateKeys account or server that stores vaults. Your vault exists only on your devices and in any backups or cloud folders you set up yourself.
support.your-vault.7: Where is the vault stored on my PC?
support.your-vault.8: In your Windows user profile, under %LOCALAPPDATA%\LocalGateKeys. Copying that file somewhere else is safe, because it is encrypted, but use scheduled backups rather than copying the live file.
support.your-vault.9: Can I import from another password manager?
support.your-vault.10: Yes. Choose Import & export in the app and pick the export file from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, Dashlane, Proton Pass, KeePass or KeePassXC (a .kdbx file opens directly), Chrome, Edge, Brave, Firefox or Safari. Any other CSV file works too: you tell the app which column is which. You review every item before anything is written, and the import never goes online. Afterwards, delete the export file, because most exports hold your passwords in plain text.
support.your-vault.11: Does it work without an internet connection?
support.your-vault.12: Yes, completely. The app uses the network only for update checks (which also fetch the licence revocation list), breach checks you start, website icons if you turn them on, and sync if you set it up. Strict offline mode, on by default, blocks background requests, website icons and breach checks and asks before an update check. See the security page.
support.filling-sign-ins.2: Why does the browser extension need the desktop app?
support.filling-sign-ins.3: The vault is kept in the desktop app, not in the browser. The extension asks the app, through a small local helper, for the logins that match the site you are on. That way the browser never holds your whole vault. Install the app first, then add the extension from the download page.
support.filling-sign-ins.5: Yes, in Chrome and Edge on Windows. When a website offers a passkey, the extension asks whether to save it in LocalGateKeys, and you approve it in the desktop app. Signing in with it works the same way. You can always choose the browser's own passkey dialog instead, or turn passkeys off in the app's autofill settings. Passkeys count as items toward the free plan's 4-item limit.
support.filling-sign-ins.6: A Windows app will not fill. Why?
support.filling-sign-ins.7: Windows app fill only works when the app exposes real sign-in fields to Windows. It will refuse when:
support.filling-sign-ins.8: the app has been updated since you bound it, so its fingerprint changed; bind it again
support.filling-sign-ins.9: the app runs as administrator and LocalGateKeys does not
support.filling-sign-ins.10: the sign-in screen is drawn by a game engine or an embedded web page that cannot be verified
support.filling-sign-ins.11: These refusals are deliberate. LocalGateKeys will not fall back to recording or simulating keystrokes blindly.
support.filling-sign-ins.13: No. It installs no keyboard hook and never watches what you type. See things LocalGateKeys never does.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.3: Unlimited items, device sync, two-factor codes and documents. The free edition holds up to 4 items: logins, notes, cards, identities and every other kind count, items in the trash do not. See pricing.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.4: What happens if I have more than 4 items without Pro?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.5: Nothing is taken away. This can happen after upgrading from an older version or after removing a licence. Every item stays usable, editable and fillable; you just cannot add a new one until you buy Pro or go back under 4.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.6: Do I have to pay again for updates?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.7: No. Pro is a single payment that includes every future update. There is no subscription and nothing to renew.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.8: How many PCs can I use Pro on?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.9: All the PCs you personally use. The licence is for one person; please buy one for each member of your household or team.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.10: How do I turn on Pro, and what if I lose my key?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.11: After payment you see your licence key straight away, with a file to download. Paste the key in Tools > Licence. The key is also saved inside your encrypted vault, so restoring a backup restores Pro. See your Pro licence.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.13: Yes, a full refund within 30 days of purchase, no questions asked. A refunded licence is revoked, so the 4-item limit applies again; every existing item stays usable. See the refund policy.
support.pro-licences-and-payment.14: Who handles the payment, and can I get an invoice?
support.pro-licences-and-payment.15: {{MERCHANT_OF_RECORD}} sells Pro on our behalf as merchant of record. They take the payment, apply the right VAT or sales tax and issue receipts and invoices, including invoices with your company's VAT number.
support.sync-and-iphone.2: Does Wi-Fi sync go over the internet?
support.sync-and-iphone.3: No. Paired PCs on the same network connect to each other directly, over a connection that is authenticated and encrypted. Both need to be unlocked. Sync is part of Pro.
support.sync-and-iphone.4: What can my cloud provider see if I sync through a cloud folder?
support.sync-and-iphone.5: Encrypted files, how many there are, their sizes and when they change, and a list of your devices' random IDs and public keys. Not the names, usernames, passwords or anything else inside your vault. Your provider's own terms apply to the files you store with them.
support.sync-and-iphone.7: Yes. Get LocalGateKeys on the App Store. It syncs with your Windows PC and, like the Windows app, collects no data.An iPhone app is coming. It will sync with your Windows PC and, like the Windows app, will collect no data.
